hero.lead: A nation of 2.4 million with farmland across three quarters of its land, where the EU’s €1.9 billion Growth Plan had made €661 million available by October 2026.

capital.heading: Paid for every reform, and a living income for every family.

register.name: Growth and Resilience Development Policy Loan
register.detail: World Bank (IBRD) · approved by the Board 4 June 2026 · P513997 · first of two operations
register.note: The first of two operations; Logos Press reports a second stage of $150 million planned for 2027
register.text: Budget support from the World Bank for reforms that integrate Moldova into EU electricity markets, modernise district heating, formalise temporary workers and widen access to early childhood education. It finances the public budget as a whole and links reform to the energy, education and livelihood standards.

register.name: Restoring Ecosystems for Marine Pollution Prevention (RE-MAP)
register.detail: World Bank · Global Environment Facility grant · approved 22 October 2025 · Dniester River Basin
register.note: About 99,200 people expected to benefit, 40% of them women
register.text: A Global Environment Facility grant, approved by the World Bank Board, to restore forests and wetlands, plant trees and spread integrated crop, livestock and forest systems that protect water resources in the Dniester River Basin. It serves the water and food standards and the incomes of rural families.

register.name: Supporting Economic Opportunities and Climate Transition DPO
register.detail: World Bank · approved 8 May 2025 · P507576 · with $7.7M in M-GROW grants and an $8M Global Concessional Financing Facility grant
register.note: The Global Concessional Financing Facility has enabled $557.91 million in World Bank loans to Moldova on concessional terms
register.text: Budget support for reforms that raise Moldova’s growth prospects and energy security in line with European Union standards, with a fair competition framework, insolvency reform and a better business environment. It finances the public budget and serves the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Strengthening Disaster Risk Management and Resilience
register.text: A World Bank operation to prepare Moldova for floods, droughts and other disasters. It protects homes, harvests and public services, serving the shelter, food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Sustainable Transition through Energy Efficiency (STEEM)
register.text: A World Bank operation to lower energy bills in public buildings and homes through energy efficiency. It serves the energy and shelter standards.

register.name: Supporting Growth and Resilience DPO
register.text: World Bank budget support for growth and resilience reforms. It finances the public budget as a whole.

register.name: Rural Connectivity Project
register.text: A World Bank project to rehabilitate and upgrade local roads with climate-resilient design and road safety measures near schools and settlements, and to modernise border crossings with Romania. It connects villages to markets and services, serving the livelihood standard.
register.note: About 95 km of three priority local roads, a new border crossing at Ungheni and modernised crossings at Giurgiulești and Leușeni

register.name: Rehabilitation of priority centralised irrigation systems
register.detail: EBRD · sovereign loan to the Government of Moldova · announced 13 October 2026 · up to €49.8M for the Puhacenii de Sus and Masivul Causeni systems, up to €53.1M for further systems · €4.8M EU Neighbourhood Investment Platform grant · up to €7.2M national contribution under the EU Growth Plan
register.note: Almost 7,000 hectares of arable land; about 13 million cubic metres of water saved a year
register.text: An EBRD loan to the Government of Moldova to rehabilitate and modernise priority centralised irrigation systems, managed with water users’ associations and farmers. It reduces farmers’ exposure to climate-related production shocks and serves the food, water and livelihood standards.

register.name: Reform and Growth Facility for Moldova
register.detail: European Commission · 2025-2027 · €289M in 2025 · €189M on 17 March 2026 after 24 reforms · €157M on 5 October 2026 after 18 reforms
register.text: The EU’s Growth Plan for Moldova, paid in grants and concessional loans against reforms in seven areas, among them social cohesion and labour markets, energy and the green transition. Of the March 2026 payment, €173 million went directly into the state budget and €16 million to projects through the Neighbourhood Investment Platform; it finances the public budget as a whole.
register.note: €661 million made available to Moldova under the Plan by 5 October 2026

register.name: Rehabilitation and modernisation of schools in Moldova
register.detail: EIB Global · loan signed at the Government 19 June 2026 · 20 schools · up to €51.5M in all, with a €3.5M EU grant and €8M from Moldova
register.note: About 40,000 pupils; the national share is supported by the Growth Plan for Moldova
register.text: An EIB loan to renovate, rebuild and modernise 20 schools, with insulation, renewable energy, heating, ventilation, lighting, fire safety and accessibility. It serves the education standard and lowers the energy bills of public schools.

register.name: Energy efficiency in public hospitals, additional EU grant
register.detail: European Union through EIB Global · 19 June 2026 · Neighbourhood Investment Platform · 10 public hospitals · €72.4M upgrade financed by the EU, the EIB and the EBRD
register.note: About 203,000 m² of hospital space renovated by the end of 2028, for a cut of about 40% in energy use
register.text: An EU investment grant, managed by EIB Global, for thermal insulation and solar panels in selected public hospitals, under the Moldova Energy Efficiency project. It lowers the running costs of hospitals and serves the health and energy standards.

register.name: Cahul regional hospital
register.detail: EIB Global · financing contract signed, announced 8 July 2025 · Ministry of Health · completion scheduled by 2030
register.note: About 300,000 people in Cahul and nearby towns, among them Comrat, Leova, Ceadir-Lunga, Taraclia, Cantemir and Vulcanesti
register.text: An EIB loan to build a new regional hospital for southern Moldova, with technical assistance from the EU, the Eastern Partnership Technical Assistance Trust Fund and Swedfund. It serves the health standard for about 300,000 people.

register.name: Chișinău district heating modernisation
register.detail: EIB Global · Termoelectrica SA · signed 8 July 2025 · co-financed by the EBRD, with EU and E5P grants · works due within seven years
register.note: About 300,000 households; 2,510 individual thermal points; 1,665 apartment buildings converted
register.text: An EIB loan to Termoelectrica, the largest heating company in Moldova, to replace vertical heating systems in apartment buildings with horizontal pipelines and install individual substations. It is projected to cut energy use by 25% and lower heating bills, serving the energy and shelter standards.

register.name: Modernisation of schools, Model Schools Network
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · signed 13 June 2025 · Ministry of Education and Research · 15 schools · €5M E5P grant for energy efficiency
register.text: A CEB loan to the Republic of Moldova to modernise 15 primary and secondary schools across the country, with full renovation, energy efficiency works, renewable energy and access for people with reduced mobility. It serves the education standard.

register.name: Moldova Energy Security 2025, Energocom
register.detail: EBRD · Board date 11 June 2025 · €300M senior working capital loan and €100M in guarantees · guaranteed by the Republic of Moldova
register.note: The Ministry of Energy reports that the financing supported the purchase of 96% of the gas for the right bank in the 2025–2026 heating season
register.text: EBRD financing for the state-owned energy trader Energocom to buy gas and electricity reserves on European markets. It keeps homes heated and lit through the winter and protects vulnerable households, serving the energy standard.

register.name: INSPIREE: energy efficiency renovation of public buildings
register.detail: Agence Française de Développement · signed at the Élysée Palace, Paris, published 11 March 2025 · Ministry of Energy · co-financed by Germany through KfW and by Moldova
register.note: Renovation of public buildings, including higher education institutions and district hospitals
register.text: A French financing agreement for the Initiative for Sustainable Public Infrastructure Development through Energy Efficiency Renovations, implemented by the Energy Projects Implementation Unit. It lowers the energy use of universities and district hospitals, serving the energy, education and health standards.

register.name: Loan to Microinvest for small businesses and farmers
register.detail: Council of Europe Development Bank · signed 29 June 2026 · first CEB loan to Microinvest
register.note: Microinvest reports more than 50,000 active clients, 17 offices and 410 professionals
register.text: A CEB loan to Microinvest, the leading non-bank lender in Moldova, for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and farmers. It aims to preserve and create jobs and develop rural communities, serving the livelihood standard.

register.name: Portfolio risk-sharing facility with maib
register.detail: EBRD · 4 June 2026 · up to €25M · unfunded guarantee on newly originated loans · first-loss cover from the EU’s EFSD+ Financial Inclusion programme
register.note: Expected to unlock up to €50 million in new lending to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises
register.text: An EBRD risk-sharing facility with maib, the largest bank in Moldova, that shares the credit risk of new loans to small businesses, among them businesses led by women and young people. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Senior loan to Microinvest
register.detail: EBRD · 27 January 2026 · up to €20M equivalent · multi-currency · Financial Intermediaries Framework
register.note: Microinvest holds 40% of the non-bank lending market and was recently bought by Victoriabank
register.text: An EBRD loan to Microinvest for on-lending to private micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in Moldova. It serves the livelihood standard by widening credit to businesses, farmers and individuals.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2025
items.text: Citizens abroad send home a steady share of the economy: a flow that can back long-term finance.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 19.5% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: Vibe Academy
items.text: A social enterprise founded in Cahul in 2019 that teaches children aged 4 to 16 programming, robotics, 3D modelling and electronics in seven centres in Cahul and branches in Chișinău, Orhei, Criuleni, Hîncești and Edineț, free of charge for children from orphanages or vulnerable families and for symbolic fees for others.

items.name: InvaLife
items.text: An association of people with motor disabilities in Tiraspol whose social enterprise rents out rehabilitation equipment, one of 23 social enterprises funded by the East Europe Foundation with EU and Swedish support that reported income from economic activities to its 2025 impact evaluation.

items.name: Floare de Cireș
items.text: A catering social enterprise founded in 2012 by the Eco-Răzeni association in Răzeni, Ialoveni district, that employs 51 people, 30 of them young people with disabilities or from disadvantaged groups, and runs a social canteen serving hot meals to hundreds of vulnerable people in three villages.

items.name: Eco Life For You (CreamBerg)
items.text: A social enterprise of the Positive Initiative association in Beriozchi, Anenii Noi district, that makes CreamBerg natural ice cream from the milk of its own mini dairy farm and employs three to six people at a time, most of them former prisoners or people who have completed rehabilitation, with 26 people released from detention helped since 2018.

items.name: Stupina cu povești
items.text: The beekeeping social enterprise of the Association of Deaf Children in Chișinău, one of 23 social enterprises funded by the East Europe Foundation with EU and Swedish support that reported income from economic activities to its 2025 impact evaluation.
